recipe: Implement an API error interceptor to centrally manage errors, using it to trigger notification toasts, log out unauthorized users, or send token refresh requests.
trigger_condition: Your React application makes API calls that can return errors requiring centralized handling.
evidence: Implement an interceptor to manage errors effectively. This interceptor can be utilized to trigger notification toasts informing users of errors, log out unauthorized users, or send requests to refresh tokens

recipe: Place multiple error boundaries in different areas of your React application rather than a single one for the entire app, so errors are contained and managed locally without disrupting the whole application.
trigger_condition: You need to handle runtime errors in React components and want to prevent one failure from crashing the entire application.
evidence: Instead of having only one error boundary for the entire app, consider placing multiple error boundaries in different areas. This way, if an error occurs, it can be contained and managed locally without disrupting the entire application's functionality

recipe: Upload source maps to Sentry so you can identify exactly where in your source code a production error occurred.
trigger_condition: You are using Sentry (or a similar tool) for production error tracking and need to locate the origin of an error in your codebase.
evidence: Make sure to upload source maps to sentry to see where in your source code did the error happen.
